dayside_temp_K.source: literature: Knutson et al. 2012, ApJ 754, 22 (arXiv:1206.6887), Sect. IV.2: dayside brightness temperature from the 4.5 um secondary eclipse depth (backend/assets/literature.toml). Spitzer IRAC 4.5 um. At 3.6 um the same paper gives 1328 +/- 11 K

host_lum_lsun.source: NASA Exoplanet Archive PSCompPars st_lum, log10 L/L_sun converted as 10^st_lum (Barstow et al. 2017)

host_mass_msun.source: NASA Exoplanet Archive PSCompPars st_mass (Stassun et al. 2017)

host_radius_rsun.source: NASA Exoplanet Archive PSCompPars st_rad (Stassun et al. 2017)

host_teff_K.source: NASA Exoplanet Archive PSCompPars st_teff (Stassun et al. 2017)

hotspot_offset_deg.source: literature: Bell et al. 2021, MNRAS 504, 3316 (arXiv:2010.00687), Table 4, HD 189733b, preferred model Poly5: offset +33.7 (+2.5 / -2.2) deg east (backend/assets/literature.toml). Spitzer IRAC 4.5 um reanalysis; err is the larger side of +2.5 / -2.2. Knutson et al. 2012 give the peak time in hours only

insolation_searth.formula: S / S_earth = (L_star / L_sun) / (a / au)^2, the flux at the planet computed by the reference from its host luminosity and orbit; not a direct measurement
insolation_searth.source: NASA Exoplanet Archive PSCompPars pl_insol (Addison et al. 2019)

mass_mearth.source: NASA Exoplanet Archive PSCompPars pl_bmasse (Stassun et al. 2017)

nightside_temp_K.source: literature: Knutson et al. 2012, ApJ 754, 22 (arXiv:1206.6887), Sect. IV.2.1: nightside brightness temperature (eclipse depth minus phase-curve amplitude) at 4.5 um (backend/assets/literature.toml). Spitzer IRAC 4.5 um. At 3.6 um the same paper gives 825 +/- 54 K. Night/day 0.78 at 4.5 um

orbit_au.source: NASA Exoplanet Archive PSCompPars pl_orbsmax (Rosenthal et al. 2021)

orbit_ecc.assumption: the reference gives e = 0 with no uncertainty, which means the orbit was fixed to a circle in its fit; read as an assumed circular orbit, not a measured eccentricity
orbit_ecc.source: NASA Exoplanet Archive PSCompPars pl_orbeccen (Stassun et al. 2017)

orbital_period_d.source: NASA Exoplanet Archive PSCompPars pl_orbper (Stassun et al. 2017)

radius_rjup.source: NASA Exoplanet Archive PSCompPars pl_radj (Stassun et al. 2017)

teq_K.assumption: the cited paper's own albedo and heat redistribution (often zero Bond albedo and full redistribution; the Kepler KOI table assumes A = 0.3; the archive row does not say which); an equilibrium temperature, not a measured one
teq_K.formula: Teq = T_star * sqrt(R_star / (2a)) * (1 - A)^(1/4), as computed in the cited paper
teq_K.source: NASA Exoplanet Archive PSCompPars pl_eqt (Addison et al. 2019)

render_params.alt_text: HD 189733 b, Gas giant, 1.13 Jupiter radii (measured), colour family from the equilibrium temperature, lit by its star. Surface relief: illustrative.

confidence.formula: C = sum(w_i c_i) / sum(w_i): c is 1 for a measured value or a formula of measured values, a placeholder share for a model-dependent one, and 0 for an assumed, artistic or missing one; the w_i are placeholder weights (D-36, Q-221)
confidence.found: Data for: Radius, mass, orbit and tides, temperature and colour.
confidence.note: This is how much of the picture rests on data. It is not the probability that the picture is correct.
confidence.weights_note: Placeholder weights: they come from the approved prototype until a sensitivity sweep replaces them (D-36).

layers.description: Number of bands from the typical spin of a giant planet and the radius (Rhines scale, A7.2): about 24 from pole to pole. The jet speed is a typical value; the exact band pattern is a seeded look.
layers.formula: bands ~ sqrt(2 Omega R / U), Omega = 2 pi / P (Rhines scale, order of magnitude only)

layers.description: Flattening of the poles from the typical spin of a giant planet, with the mean density of Jupiter assumed (A7.2).
layers.formula: f = f_J (P_J / P)^2, from f = 0.7 q with q proportional to Omega^2

layers.description: Colour family chosen by the equilibrium temperature (A7.2).
layers.formula: palette family chosen by teq_K between the stops 60, 100, 130, 200, 600, 1100, 1800 K

layers.description: A few storms between the jets, as on the giant planets of the Solar System. How many and where is a seeded look; no measurement of this planet's storms is used.
Swirling detail along the band edges. Look only.

rgb.source: neutral stand-in swatch (R7.7); the drawn palette is the colour layer (A7.2)
